newsitem.title: CHINA: HSBC to do first yuan business Thursday.
newsitem.headline: HSBC to do first yuan business Thursday.

text.p: The Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp will make its first local Chinese currency loan for over four decades on Thursday from its new branch in Shanghai's Pudong district, a bank official said on Wednesday.
A Hongkong bank official in Shanghai said the bank would be executing its first loan to customers in local Chinese currency, but he declined to give details.
It is possible the loan will be the first by any foreign bank since the Chinese banking authorities approved the first batch of banks to do local currency business in December.
The head of the Shanghai branch of the People's Bank of China, Mao Yingliang, told a seminar on Wednesday that two banks would begin yuan business before the end of the week, but did not name them.
Banking analysts have said the other bank given the go-ahead is the Industrial Bank of Japan, but a senior manager with the bank in Shanghai would only say: "We won't deny it."
The Hongkong Bank official said the money for its first yuan loans would be foreign exchange brought in to China and exchanged.
"But this is just a one-off deal," he said.
"In future, loans need to be made on the basis of yuan deposits received, otherwise you are entering into a potential foreign exchange mismatch (if the exchange rates move)," he said.
